title: [D7 Emit] Sink view and the field-level output message shape
summary: `sql/migrations/0019_sink.sql` is `helena_analytical_sink`, the plain view `concept/03` asks for by name — the terminal run of a pass (analyst where it escalated, triage otherwise) joined to the triage decision beside it, to the context AT THE VERSION THE RUN RECORDED, to its entities and their enrichment evidence, and to the citation rows. `helena.sink` is the message shape field by field (`OutputMessage` and seven nested models) plus `SinkStore`, which assembles one message per terminal outcome out of that view and the four child tables of 0018. Nothing emits: that is task 47.
assumption_validated: Two, both measured against the pinned engine rather than reasoned about. (1) THE SINK CANNOT BE A `CREATE SINK`, and D7's shape follows from that: `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW ... AS SELECT ... FROM helena_analytical_enriched_context` is rejected with `Bind error: failed to bind view helena_analytical_enriched_context`, because that view derives `status` from `now()` and a streaming query refuses `now()` outside a WHERE clause. So everything downstream of the enriched context is a batch read, emission is deterministic code producing over the Kafka wire protocol, and the engine-side count is a batch SELECT. (2) NOTHING IN THE MESSAGE EXISTS ONLY IN THE TOPIC, executed rather than asserted: every field of every nested object is recovered by a query written against the underlying tables — never against the sink view — and compared, over a real pass stored by the real writer. Two fields are code-owned (`message_version`, `caveat`) and a test refuses a third.
makes_buildable: Task 47 (emission) gets the whole engine side already built and already counted: `sink.SinkStore(connection, identity).terminal()` is exactly the set of messages `concept/03` requires to be emitted (one per terminal outcome, an escalated pass appearing once and under the analyst's identifier), `.pending()` is the engine-side count at message grain, and `.project(assessment_id)` returns the validated `OutputMessage` to serialize. `OutputMessage.assessment_id` is the deduplication key the consumer contract will be written against — a digest over (tenant, sensor, context_id, context_version, emitter, trigger), stable across a re-run. The one thing task 47 must NOT do is build a RisingWave Kafka sink; ADR-0036 §2 has the measurement. Task 48 (metrics) gets `helena_analytical_sink` as an existing analytical join it can aggregate, and the `MAY_READ` change that lets an analytical view read the assessment tables at all. Task 51 (secrets hygiene) gets `OutputMessage` as the concrete shape for its 'no credential can reach an emitted message' test, and ADR-0036 §5 plus `docs/runbook.md` §11 as the statement of what the payload does carry. Task 52 (end-to-end) gets the drain target's shape.

verification.detail: 1696 passed in 549 s, full suite, against a pinned RisingWave 3.0.3 started by the session fixtures. tests/test_sink.py is 23 tests and every integration one executes the new view: the capture goes through the real normalizer (re-stamped into the live window, because helena_signal_host_context_live is bounded by the retention horizon and the committed capture is dated 2024-06-01), the ThreatFox extract through the real loader with one entry repointed at a domain the capture really has, and the assessment through the real orchestration.AssessmentStore. Covered by execution: a triage-only pass, an escalated pass emitted once with the triage decision beside it, a typed failure emitted with no verdict and model_version NULL, `ok`+claim, `ok`+`no_match`, `stale`+claim, `failed`, `missing`, an entity with an empty evidence tuple (no feed ever loaded), a context whose version has moved on (context_resolved false), the triage half of an escalated pass refused, another tenant's assessment refused, pending() counting messages and not the view's 300-odd rows, and the field-by-field recovery of every field of the fullest message there is. `uv run python -m compileall -q src tests scripts` and `uv lock --check` both clean. No new dependency, so uv.lock is unchanged.

escalations.detail: `helena.migrations.MAY_READ["analytical"]` changed from {signal, reference} to {analytical, signal, reference}. NOT a change to the invariant: `concept/instruction.md` §2 and `concept/03` both state it as 'an analytical view never reads the flatten layer or the source directly', and neither says anything about a layer reading itself — `signal` and `reference` have both been able to since MAY_READ existed. The analytical row was narrower only because until 0018 the layer held one object, and a view joining the assessment rows (analytical) to the enriched context (analytical) has nowhere else to read from. The invariant is still executed: tests/test_view_layering.py still builds an analytical view over the flatten layer and the source and asserts both named as violations. Recorded in ADR-0036 §3. Flagged rather than made silently, because it is an edit to a rule rather than to code.

Five `Read by:` declarations in already-applied migrations were edited to name helena_analytical_sink — 0009 (host_context_live), 0010 (context_entities), 0015 (enriched_context) and 0018 (assessment, citation). tests/test_view_layering.py::test_every_relation_that_reads_an_object_is_named_in_its_read_by requires it, and the checksum ledger is over the bytes, so a store migrated before 0019 must be dropped and re-migrated. This is the same standing cost `Superseded by:` already carries and the same act task 17 and 0010 already performed; docs/runbook.md §5 now names 0019 in that list and says why the cost is deliberate.

deferred: EMISSION. Nothing produces to a topic, opens a broker connection or counts what was delivered — task 47. `SinkStore.pending` is the engine-side half only, and rows the view produced is not messages that arrived. The deduplication contract for consumers and the output-volume hazard are task 47's steps, not this one's.

A VERSIONED `helena.sink.v1` MODULE, deliberately not built. The criterion docs/decisions/0008 gives for a frozen version module is that a stored row records the version and replay validates against it; no row records a message version, there is no column for one, and replay reads the assessment tables and never the topic. So `MESSAGE_VERSION` is an INTERFACE version — a change to the field set, a field's type or a field's meaning bumps it and comes with a decision record — pinned by tests/fixtures/sink/message-v1.json rather than by a module the loader resolves. A versioned package would also have forced edits to two tests in tests/test_package_layout.py, because `sink` is a COMPONENT (concept/03 names it) and that file makes components top-level modules and versioned packages directories. ADR-0036 §7 has the argument and what would reverse it.

THE ESCALATION RECORD, still unowned three tasks after task 43 left it. `Escalation.thresholds_version` reaches no row, so the message says an analyst ran on `deterministic_signal` and cannot say which thresholds decided that. Unchanged by this increment and now visible in the payload as well as in the store.

THE COMPOSITION RULE'S DECISION AND PROPOSED CLAIMS. Neither is stored (there is no findings table — tasks 43 and 45), so `OutputMessage.classification` is what the MODEL said and the message cannot carry what the evidence permitted. A field for it would be a field with no row behind it, which the recoverability rule forbids. This is the most consequential thing the message does not carry.

REDACTION. None is performed and none is planned in the sink: the broker is local, and redacting here would make the consumer's copy differ from the stored rows for no benefit. What is built instead is the statement — `MESSAGE_CAVEAT` is a field on every message, ADR-0036 §5 names the four kinds of sensitive content the payload carries, and docs/runbook.md §11 is the operator-facing version. The pipeline cannot enforce the obligation and the message does not pretend it can.

TELLING 'THE CONTEXT WAS EVICTED' FROM 'THE CONTEXT VERSION MOVED ON'. `context_resolved = FALSE` covers both: the live view no longer shows that (context_id, context_version), whether because a late record changed the digest or because the retention horizon dropped it. Distinguishing them needs the freeze-a-cited-context work concept/08 still lists as open.

ANY CONSUMER. Nothing has read one of these messages and no schema has been negotiated with anything outside this repository, so the interface is exercised by this project's tests and by nothing else. helena.sink's maturity label says `experimental` and says exactly that.
lessons: THE ENRICHED CONTEXT CANNOT BE THE SOURCE OF A STREAMING JOB, AND THAT DECIDES D7'S SHAPE. Measured 2026-09-11 on RisingWave 3.0.3: `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW probe AS SELECT context_id, status FROM helena_analytical_enriched_context` fails with `Bind error: failed to bind view helena_analytical_enriched_context`, because the view derives `status` from `now()` and `now()` outside a WHERE clause is rejected in a streaming query — the same thing sql/migrations/0009 measured for `completeness`. So there is no `CREATE SINK ... FROM helena_analytical_sink`; emission is Python reading a batch view and producing over the Kafka protocol. What DOES work in a batch view, checked at the same time: `array_agg(row(...))`, `jsonb_build_object`, `to_jsonb`, correlated self LEFT JOINs and `split_part`.

THE SINK TAKES ITS ENTITY LIST FROM `helena_signal_context_entities` AND NOT FROM THE ENRICHED CONTEXT, for the reason src/helena/rendering/__init__.py already gives: the enriched context CROSS JOINs the snapshot ledger, so on a deployment where no feed has ever loaded it yields NO ROWS AT ALL, and a message built on it would say a host contacted nothing when the only fault is that no loader has run. That turns into a FIFTH kind of absence in the emitted evidence — an entity whose evidence tuple is empty — which is not `missing` (a source that was asked for and had nothing to look in) and not `no_match` (a source that answered).

JOIN AN ASSESSMENT TO ITS CONTEXT ON `(context_id, context_version)` AND NOT ON THE ID ALONE. `context_version` is a digest over the context's own counters (0009), so a window that gained a late record has a different version under the same id, and joining on the id would put a later version's entities beside an earlier version's verdict. The sink carries `context_resolved` to say which happened, because an empty entity list that meant 'the store moved on' and an empty entity list that meant 'the host contacted nothing' would be the same bytes.

`helena_signal_host_context_live` IS BOUNDED BY THE RETENTION HORIZON (`window_end > now() - 24 hours`), SO THE COMMITTED CAPTURE'S OWN TIMESTAMPS ARE OUTSIDE IT. Any test that needs a live context has to re-stamp the records into the current window, which is what tests/test_rendering.py's `live` fixture does and what tests/test_sink.py now does. A test that ingests the capture as-is and then asks the live view for a context gets nothing and the failure reads as 'the capture produced no context'.

`tests/test_assessment_replay.py::test_the_column_list_is_the_one_the_engine_holds` QUERIES `information_schema.columns` WITHOUT A `table_schema = current_schema()` FILTER, so it fails if any OTHER schema on the same engine holds a `helena_analytical_assessment` — which is what a scratch schema left behind by an interactive session is. Two suite failures in this session (that one and tests/test_rendering.py::test_a_citation_resolves_to_evidence_the_rendering_actually_showed) were exactly this and nothing to do with the increment. Drop scratch schemas before running the suite, or add the filter.

PINNING A PYDANTIC MODEL'S `model_json_schema()` BYTE FOR BYTE PINS ITS DOCSTRINGS TOO — they arrive as `description` keys. A pin that turns every comment improvement into an 'interface change' teaches whoever hits it to regenerate the fixture reflexively, which is a pin that has stopped working. tests/test_sink.py::message_shape strips every `description` before comparing, so what is pinned is the field set, the types and which fields are required, which is what the interface actually is.
failed_approaches: AGGREGATING THE WHOLE MESSAGE IN SQL — one row per message with the entities, evidence, citations, gaps, patterns, retrievals and disclosures as `jsonb_agg` / `array_agg(row(...))` columns. The engine supports all of it in a batch query (probed before it was rejected, not after), and it would have made the sink view's row count equal the message count directly. Rejected because it puts the message's field names in SQL and the message's shape in Python, which is two copies of an interface that can disagree — and the one that goes stale is the one with no validator. The view stays at the join's natural grain and Pydantic is where the shape is checked.

A VERSIONED `helena/sink/` PACKAGE with `v1.py` holding the message classes, on the pattern of contracts/rendering/triage/analyst. Abandoned before it was written, for two reasons that are both structural: no stored row records a message version, so there is nothing for a frozen module to be resolved BY (docs/decisions/0008's own criterion), and tests/test_package_layout.py makes COMPONENT_MODULES top-level .py files and VERSIONED_PACKAGES directories — `sink` is a component concept/03 names, so it cannot be both without restructuring that test. The interface version plus a pinned schema fixture does the job the task asked for at a fraction of the structure.

PUTTING `status` ON `EmittedEvidence` AS `str | None` to leave room for 'no source has ever been asked'. Wrong shape: when no source has been asked there is no evidence ROW at all, so the nullable field could only ever have been filled by a join producing a row about a source it could not name. It is `str` and required, the absence is an empty `evidence` tuple, and a NULL is now a loud validation failure rather than a sixth meaning nobody declared.
next_session_should_know: Task 47 is emission and everything on the engine side is built. EIGHT THINGS TO CARRY. (1) DO NOT WRITE A `CREATE SINK`. It cannot be built over this view — the enriched context derives `status` from `now()` and a streaming query rejects that, measured and quoted in ADR-0036 §2. Emission is `helena.broker` producing what `SinkStore.project` returns, which also keeps concept/instruction.md §2's 'the broker is addressed only through the Kafka wire protocol, on both ends' true with one Kafka client rather than two mechanisms. (2) THE THREE CALLS ARE `SinkStore(connection=, identity=).terminal() -> tuple[str, ...]`, `.pending() -> int` and `.project(assessment_id) -> OutputMessage`. `terminal()` is already exactly 'one per terminal outcome' — the view picks the analyst row where a pass escalated and the triage row otherwise, so an escalated context appears ONCE and under the analyst's identifier. `project` refuses the triage half of an escalated pass and another tenant's assessment, loudly, and both refusals have tests. (3) THE DEDUPLICATION KEY IS `OutputMessage.assessment_id` and the consumer contract should say so: it is a digest over (tenant, sensor, context_id, context_version, emitter, trigger) with no outcome in it, so a re-run of the same snapshot mints the same key and discarding a repeat is correct rather than lossy. (4) `pending()` COUNTS DISTINCT ASSESSMENT IDS, NOT VIEW ROWS. The view's grain is (terminal run x entity x source) and a real context produces a few hundred rows per message; counting rows would make 'nothing arrived' impossible to tell from 'one message arrived', which is the exact thing concept/03 says the count exists to prevent. (5) IF YOU ADD A FIELD TO `OutputMessage`, THREE TESTS FIRE AND ALL THREE ARE RIGHT: the recovery-route map (`RECOVERED_FROM` in tests/test_sink.py) refuses a field with no engine relation behind it, the executed recovery test refuses one that does not match its rows, and the pinned schema fixture refuses the shape change. The fix is a `MESSAGE_VERSION` bump plus a new `message-vN.json` plus a decision record — tests/fixtures/sink/README.md says it and says regenerating the old file is the one wrong answer. (6) THE PROSE IS NOT PINNED, ONLY THE STRUCTURE. `tests/test_sink.py::message_shape` strips every `description` from the JSON Schema before comparing, so editing a docstring does not fail the test. That was deliberate — see the lessons. (7) `MAY_READ["analytical"]` NOW INCLUDES `analytical`, and `helena_analytical_sink` is the first object anywhere to read its own layer. The invariant is untouched and still executed; ADR-0036 §3 is the record. If you add another analytical view, remember the `Read by:` retrofit — tests/test_view_layering.py fails until every relation you read names you, and that means editing already-applied migration files, which invalidates their checksums (docs/runbook.md §5). (8) THE MESSAGE CARRIES UNREDACTED INTERNAL ADDRESSES, HOSTNAMES, RETRIEVED EXTERNAL TEXT AND A DISCLOSURE LEDGER, and every message says so in its own `caveat` field. docs/runbook.md §11 is the operator-facing statement; a SIEM forwarder or cloud connector on this topic is an egress decision under concept/instruction.md §3, not a configuration detail. Task 51's 'no credential can reach an emitted message' test has `OutputMessage` to write against now.
